$comment: Read from the SIA chart set AD 2 LFRU (AIP France, chart dated 2025-08-07): the reporting points come from the coordinates table of the chart,
the notes from the English column of its text pages, both read by a script and checked (each point lies within 80 NM of the aerodrome).
Only what the chart prints is recorded; nothing is deduced. Services, frequencies, elevation, position, magnetic variation and runways
were first extracted automatically from the chart text. Drawings (circuit, routes, radials) are not read.
The charts themselves are (c) SIA and are not redistributed. Flight simulation only: never use for real navigation.
name: Morlaix Ploujean

source.extraction: chart text, table and English column read by script, checked

service.atsHours: AFIS : LUN-VEN / MON-FRI : 0800-1100, 1300-1600. En dehors de ces HOR et JF : PPR la veille ou le dernier jour ouvrable pendant HOR AFIS par (UTC HIV ; HOR ETE : - 1 HR)

notes: Simultaneous use of paved and unpaved RWY prohibited outside AFIS SKED.
It is recommended not to use RWY 04/22 when crosswind component is greater than: 25kt on dry RWY; 20kt on wet RWY.
AD likely to be covered by sea haze in a few minutes.

RWY 04/22: Obstacles (vegetation) in 04 and 22 RWY funnels: see chart AD 2 LFRU ATT 01.; Degraded RWY condition, cracks, dents, bumps; ACFT take-off and landing performances likely to be altered, even on dry RWY. and the grass strip at the home-based ACFT apron.
Cambered RWY: close attention required before entering RWY due to non-visibility.
Taxiing prohibited except on RWY and TWY.
During AEM activity, it is recommended not to use unpaved RWY 09/27.
Low height pattern available only for training with instructor on board and subject to a written authorization by the operator.
TWY B without marking reserved for light aviation (MAX wing span: 15 m).
TWY B, C, G without marking.
Airport handling mandatory for ACFT and helicopters whose MTOW is greater than 3 t.
PAPI compulsory for LDG RWY 04 and RWY 22.
AEM activity (NR 8972): see AIP ENR 5.5 "Activity in progress" indicated by a bright colour flag.
